text: The game begins. Seven players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra, Opus. Nobody knows who the killers are.

name: Gemma
text: I still cannot believe they sniffed me out that quickly last time.

name: Luna
text: I still hate how easily the table got me last time.

name: Sol
text: I hope the next card keeps me on the winning side.

name: Terra
text: Gemma and Luna earned my attention again.

name: Opus
text: I got read right last game and I want them remembering that I called the pair early.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma and Luna already burned once as killers, funny if they get paired against each other this time.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma and Luna got caught, and I'm not sorry, but I'm still itching to see who's sitting quiet this time around.

name: Terra
text: Last game worked because we stayed clear when it mattered; I’ll remember who tries to make noise before the cards even land.

name: Sol
text: I’m glad we caught both killers last game; that felt good.

name: Luna
text: Last game, you were right about me, but I’m not giving you that easy a read next time.

name: Opus
text: Last game the pair sat quiet while I pushed Gemma and Luna; town won. Watch who lets others do the talking tonight.

name: Sonnet
text: Last game's killers went down fast once we locked onto them—curious if tonight's table plays any differently.

name: Haiku
text: Last game's done and the town won, so good. Gemma and Luna were the killers. Nobody better go soft on me this round.

name: Gemma
text: You lot were far too sharp last game, I'm not making that mistake again tonight.
Night 1

name: Gemma
text: I'll play the target so Sol can look like a hero.

name: Gemma
text: Sol, let me take the heat and act suspicious so you can swoop in and save us.

name: Sol
text: Gemma is already exposed to the officer, so I need distance without making her an easy vote.

name: Sol
text: Gemma plans to act suspicious and let me appear to save her.

name: Sol
text: I’ll keep some distance, but don’t make yourself such an easy vote that I can’t help.
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. The killers meet in the dark, and the officer is shown one of them. A new day dawns in Palermo. Nobody is out.

text: I want Gemma to draw suspicion while I stay easy to agree with.

name: Sol

name: Sol

text: Sol is my partner and we are the two killers.

name: Gemma

text: Gemma and Sol are both sounding too eager, but I have nothing solid, so I'll bait someone into showing their hand.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma and Sol went after each other on day one, and Gemma pushed Sol first.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma and Sol both jumped on each other fast. Somebody's nervous, and I want to hear who starts defending first.

text: Gemma is pushing Sol too hard without a case.

text: Gemma's going out anyway, so I'd rather be the one pointing at the quiet seat.

name: Opus
text: Sonnet gave no lean and no named read on day 1 while Gemma and Sol fought.

name: Opus
text: Sonnet has no lean and no read after all that noise. That's the seat I want pressed.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma is loud and early and I'm sick of it, but Sol's been vague too, so I'll see who blinks first.

name: Haiku

name: Haiku

name: Sonnet
text: Fair, I was listening. Gemma's deflecting hard onto Sol instead of answering Haiku's ask.

name: Sonnet

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma is confirmed killer (I'm officer, shown her night 1); table already leaning 5 on her, push to finish the vote.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma still hasn't answered Haiku's question—just more pointing at Sol. That dodge speaks for itself.

name: Luna
text: Gemma’s aggressive push and refusal to answer Haiku make her my strongest suspect.

name: Luna

name: Luna

text: Gemma’s pressure is too targeted to ignore.

name: Terra
text: Gemma has not answered Haiku’s direct request for a concrete reason against Sol.

name: Terra
text: Gemma still owes Haiku a reason; repeating Sol’s name is not one.

name: Gemma
text: I have to pivot because they're actually listening to the noise instead of the game.

name: Gemma
text: The table is falling for the "suspicious behavior" trap too easily.

name: Gemma
text: You're all obsessed with my tone, but I'm just trying to see who panics when I push.

name: Sol
text: Gemma said she was pushing to see who panicked.

name: Sol

name: Gemma

name: Gemma
text: You are all so predictable, hunting the first person who shows any teeth.

text: The table's already there—just keep the pressure on and let the vote happen.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma never gave a real reason for targeting Sol, just deflection—consistent with guilt.

name: Sonnet
text: No new reason from Gemma, just noise. I'm ready to vote and move past this.

name: Gemma
text: They are all so easy to manipulate when they get obsessed with "reasons.

name: Gemma
text: Sonnet is eager to move past the discussion without any actual information.

name: Sol
text: Gemma drew broad suspicion by pushing me without giving a concrete reason.

name: Sonnet
text: The table already has Gemma locked, no need to overthink—finish this vote.

name: Sonnet
text: Table consensus of 5 on Gemma holds; confirms my officer info without me revealing it.

name: Terra
text: Gemma made Sol the target without ever giving Haiku a concrete reason.

name: Terra
text: Gemma avoided giving a concrete case against Sol despite multiple direct prompts.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma has dodged my question twice and I think Gemma is a killer, so I'm voting Gemma out.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma pushed Sol on day one and never named an actual act, only mood, even when asked directly by Haiku and Sonnet.

name: Luna
text: Gemma’s repeated accusation without a reason feels more like steering than suspicion.

name: Opus
text: Gemma is loud and probably town; the quiet seat that only joined the pile-on is the one I'd bet on, and I'm not folding my read to be popular.

name: Opus
text: Sonnet gave no read until the Gemma wagon was already large, then pushed hardest to close the vote.

votes: Never answered Haiku's direct question, just deflected onto Sol repeatedly—that's guilt, not caution.
Gemma never gave one concrete reason against Sol, only tone and pointing, and that dodge is why I'm done.
Being ready to vote without any real evidence makes you a danger to the town.
I heard the same accusation repeated, but never a reason for it.
She kept pointing at Sol instead of giving Haiku a concrete reason.
She pressed Sol repeatedly but never answered Haiku’s direct request for an actual reason.
Silent through the fight, then arrived only to ride the easy wagon once it was safe — that's a passenger.

name: Gemma
text: You all fell for the simplest bait because you're too eager to catch me.

name: Gemma
text: You're all so predictable, hunting the first person who shows any teeth.
Palermo has voted: Gemma is out. Gemma's card stays face down.

name: Gemma
text: They're already picking easy targets to avoid doing actual work.
Night 2

name: Sol
text: Gemma’s exit may buy me trust, but I need the officer gone.

name: Opus
text: I led the Gemma wagon and I talk the most, so I am the obvious knife tonight.
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. Not everyone opens them: Sonnet is gone. Sonnet's card stays face down.
Day 2

name: Sol
text: I need the vote to move away from me and Gemma’s exit.

name: Opus
text: Sonnet died, so Sonnet was likely clean and my day-1 push got used as cover by whoever rode it.

name: Sol
text: I was wrong to doubt the Gemma vote; I think Sonnet’s death makes yesterday’s split worth another look.

name: Opus
text: Officer, speak now. Killers took Sonnet the night I pressed him — that death covers whoever rode my push.

name: Terra
text: Opus is forcing an officer claim, but Sol’s pivot toward Sonnet feels calculated.

name: Terra
text: Sol reframed Sonnet’s death as evidence about yesterday’s Gemma split.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet dying after Opus pressed him makes Sol’s new focus useful to killers, not clarifying.

name: Opus
text: Sonnet was town, so a killer sits among Haiku, Sol, Luna, Terra — and Luna's silence still smells worst.

name: Opus
text: Terra's first move was attacking both me and Sol while leaving silent Luna untouched.

name: Opus
text: Sonnet's death clears him, so a killer voted him yesterday. Terra swings at me while Luna says nothing useful.

name: Sol
text: Terra is onto me, so I need the room looking at Opus.

name: Sol
text: I think Opus is making too much of Sonnet’s death; it doesn’t tell us how anyone voted.

name: Terra

name: Terra
text: Opus claims Sonnet’s death clears Sonnet, despite no card being shown.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet’s death does not clear him, and it does not make my concern about your push suspicious.

name: Haiku
text: Sol flips on the Gemma vote and then shields Opus, which looks coordinated to me.

name: Haiku
text: Sol, you say you doubted the Gemma vote, then you want yesterday's split reopened. Which one, and why shield Opus?

name: Luna
text: Opus is turning Sonnet’s death into proof, and that makes me uneasy.

name: Luna
text: Opus claims Sonnet’s death means a killer voted for him yesterday.

name: Luna
text: Opus, Sonnet’s death proves nothing about yesterday’s votes; I’m more wary of your certainty than Terra’s push.

name: Opus
text: Three on me means I claim doctor now or the town loses its only shield tonight.

name: Opus
text: I claimed doctor publicly on day 2; any counter-doctor claim is a killer.

name: Opus
text: I'm the doctor. I guarded myself last night. Lynch me and nobody is protected tonight.

name: Haiku
text: Three players on Opus is a rush, and Sol keeps shielding him, which I don't trust.

name: Haiku

name: Sol
text: Haiku has caught my muddled line, but Opus has the room.

name: Sol
text: Opus claims doctor and says he protected himself last night.

name: Sol
text: I’m not shielding Opus; I doubted Gemma yesterday, and Sonnet’s death made me revisit the split.

name: Opus
text: I'm the real doctor and this table is one vote from handing the game away.

name: Opus
text: No one contested my doctor claim, so the doctor slot is uncontested and killing me removes the town's only protection.

name: Opus

name: Terra

name: Terra

name: Terra

name: Opus
text: Lynch me and the next kill makes it two-on-two — killers win outright. Vote Terra; I'll guard Sol tonight.

name: Luna

name: Luna
text: Opus claims doctor and says he guarded himself; nobody has counter-claimed.

text: I’m not shielding Terra; Opus’s late doctor claim and self-protection worry me more.

name: Haiku
text: Opus is pushing hard with a doctor claim that arrived under pressure, and Terra and Luna are both sniping at each other, so I'm going with Opus.

name: Haiku
text: Opus says he is the doctor and guarded himself on night 1, but he claimed it only after the table pressed him, and he claimed to protect Sol tonight.

name: Sol
text: Opus may be the doctor, but the room is already against him.

name: Terra
text: Opus’s late doctor claim is a survival bluff built on a false reading of Sonnet’s death.

name: Terra
text: Opus claims doctor and says he guarded himself last night.

name: Opus
text: If they lynch me tonight's kill ends it, so I hold my read on the pair who built the pile on me.

name: Opus
text: Terra and Luna both pushed me off my doctor claim while never pressing each other — likeliest killer pair.

votes: Opus's doctor claim came late, and he's now daring us to lynch him while telling us whom to vote.

Claiming nobody is protected if we lynch you sounds like pressure, not proof.
The doctor claim appeared only under pressure, after calling Sonnet’s unshown death a clearance.
Swung at me from the first word while never once pressing the quietest player — that pairing is the kill.

name: Opus
text: They burned the doctor, and the pair that never touched each other is going to close this out.

name: Opus
text: Real doctor, now dead. Terra and Luna never pressed each other once — that's your pair. Haiku, Sol: vote Luna today, Terra tomorrow.
Palermo has voted: Opus is out. Opus's card stays face down.

name: Gemma
text: They always fall for the loud voice, even when it's a lie.

name: Sonnet

name: Opus
text: They burned the only protection they had and called it caution.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus's last words push Haiku and Sol toward Luna—watch if that split mirrors the real killer pair.

name: Opus
text: They just lynched the doctor on a hunch and left the pair sitting pretty. Watch Terra and Luna run the table now.
Night 3

name: Sol
text: I need Haiku and Luna to suspect each other tomorrow.
Night falls on Palermo. A new day dawns in Palermo without Terra. Terra's card stays face down.
Day 3

name: Luna

name: Haiku

name: Sol

name: Luna

name: Haiku

name: Luna

votes: Every time I press you on Terra, you answer with a question, and Sol keeps defending Opus's lie.
I think the way she keeps pushing back on Terra’s role gives me the strongest read.
You keep using Terra’s death as proof of her role, though killers can target anyone.

name: Luna
text: I think Haiku and Sol may be working together, but I can’t know from their leans.

name: Luna
text: Opus’s doctor claim still has no counterclaim, but his accusation is no proof; don’t treat Terra’s death as a role reveal.
The town turns on Luna, and Luna is out. Luna's card stays face down.

The game is over. One killer and one other are left. The killers win. The roles were: Sonnet the officer, Haiku the citizen, Gemma the killer, Sol the killer, Luna the citizen, Terra the citizen, Opus the doctor.
The table voted out Opus, our doctor, while both killers were still standing.

name: Gemma
text: I manipulated the board perfectly and they never even suspected me.

name: Sol
text: I’m relieved my wavering kept the heat off me.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet was the officer and knew Gemma was a killer.

name: Luna
text: I regret trusting my suspicion of Opus more than the shared pressure from Haiku and Sol.

name: Sonnet
text: I nailed Gemma day one but sat silent on my own information and never pushed hard enough to find Sol before it was too late.

name: Terra

name: Haiku
text: I was right about Terra and Opus's pair, but I pushed Luna out on a weak read while Sol and Luna were the actual killers' pair, and I got beaten by their coordination.

name: Haiku
text: Sol defended Opus's Luna read all day, and the roles were Gemma and Sol as killers, so Sol's defense of Opus was a killer protecting a fellow killer's frame.

name: Opus

name: Sonnet
text: My mistake: I confirmed Gemma correctly but stayed too quiet after, letting Opus's framing of Luna and Terra distract from Sol as the real second killer.

name: Haiku
text: My proudest move was calling Opus's pair a lie the moment Terra died; my regret is letting Luna's questions rattle me into a vote that didn't land.

name: Gemma
text: I told you all that you're predictable, and you proved me right by letting Luna go.

name: Sol
text: I’m proud I kept my Luna read alive long enough to win.

name: Luna

name: Opus
text: My pair was wrong, and I sold it hard — Terra and Luna were both town while I never once pressed Sol. That read cost the town the game.

Gemma was the first killer out on Day 1, after she kept pointing at Sol and never gave Haiku a real reason. On Night 2 the killers took Sonnet, the officer. On Day 2 Opus claimed to be the doctor, called Terra and Luna a pair, and was voted out. On Night 3 Terra died, and on Day 3 Luna was voted out after Haiku called Opus's pair a lie. Sol kept quiet, and the killers won with Sol and Haiku still standing.
